messages:
ops-bot: [ALERT] inference-api:5xx-rate > 5% for 3m — paging maya (oncall) :rotating_light:

maya (oncall): seeing the page. I'm jumping in. any immediate customer tickets?

lia (support): no high-sev customer tickets yet, but a couple of embed requests timed out earlier. I flagged two customers (acct-239, acct-880) just in case.

maya (oncall): ok starting triage — checking grafana and the runtime pods. @jun can you look at infra metrics (node OOMs / network)? Sam can you watch model-serving logs?

jun (sre): looking. nodes look healthy, no OOMs. network egress spikes are normal. noticing a lot of small concurrent requests to /v1/embeddings from a single client IP range. could be a traffic burst that pushed queueing.

sam (eng-runtime): logs show increased backend latency around 09:13 UTC, KV cache misses spiked. A few workers reported transient resource exhaustion while rebuilding cache for a hot model (open-model-7b).

maya (oncall): root hypothesis: sudden concurrent prefixes causing cache rebuilds -> increased token latency -> 5xx backpressure. Mitigation plan: 1) throttle that client hit by rate-limit rule 2) enable short-term maintenance silence for the noisy alert so paging doesn't recur during mitigation 3) bump autoscale min for affected pool.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by maya (oncall).

maya (oncall): lia please escalate to the two flagged customers proactively with a short note: "We observed transient errors in embeddings; we're mitigating — expect reduced error rate in ~20m."

lia (support): will send messages now. crafting short msg: "Hi — we briefly saw errors for embedding calls; our on-call has throttled high concurrent clients and put mitigations in place. We'll update in 30m."

jun (sre): I'm creating a temporary Grafana silence and a Prometheus silence for the alert to avoid repeats while we validate. Also capturing the alert spike for post-incident review.

sam (eng-runtime): Applying an emergency config: toggle soft-cache-rebuild to serialize rebuilds (reduces parallel rebuilds). Pushing change to canary: 

```json
{
  "service": "runtime",
  "feature_toggle": "soft_cache_rebuild",
  "value": "on",
  "reason": "mitigate concurrent cache rebuild storms"
}
```

maya (oncall): nice. jun, can you add a temporary rate-limit rule for that client IP range? Something like: max 50 concurrent embedding requests per minute.

jun (sre): rate-limit rule deployed as a quick ACL on the edge for the offending CIDR. Also created a short maintenance window in PagerDuty for this incident (20m).

ops-bot: Silence created for alert: inference-api:5xx-rate (duration=30m) by jun (sre).

maya (oncall): monitoring graphs look better after rate-limit and serialized rebuilds. 5xx down to 0.7% at 09:27 UTC. customer messages sent. moving to recovery and cleanup phase.

sam (eng-runtime): confirm: I've made the soft-cache-rebuild change reversible and put a flag in the config so we can revert after validation. I'll open a PR with the change and the canary verification steps. link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/412

jun (sre): for post-incident: propose the following alert tuning steps: 
- lower sensitivity of current alert to 10m window (prevent flapping for brief bursts)
- add an additional alert "embedding-queue-depth > X" to catch queueing before 5xxs
- add dashboard panel showing KV cache rebuild rate + cache miss ratio per model

maya (oncall): agreed. also add a permanent automation: if cache-rebuild-rate > Y then automatically throttle new connections to that model for 60s.

lia (support): will follow up with the two customers and close the loop once we have finalized post-incident actions.

maya (oncall): post-incident checklist (we should complete before declaring RCA):
1) Create incident summary & timeline (I'll draft)
2) Open follow-up tickets for alert rule updates and dashboard work (jun/sam own)
3) Validate new thresholds during a planned load test (eng-runtime to run)
4) Remove silences and maintenance windows after validations
5) Update runbook to include cache rebuild mitigation steps and automatic throttling behavior

jun (sre): created tasks: 
- RFC: alert-sensitivity-adjustments (#RST-119)
- Dashboards: add-cache-metrics (#MON-402)
- Automation: model-throttle-on-rebuild (#AUT-77)
Links: https://tickets.internal/PROJECTS/RST-119, https://tickets.internal/PROJECTS/MON-402, https://tickets.internal/PROJECTS/AUT-77

sam (eng-runtime): I'll run a controlled replay of the burst pattern in staging with KV cache monitoring. plan to test two thresholds for auto-throttle (20s vs 60s) and capture false-positive rate.

maya (oncall): timeline: we'll keep the silence active until we validate (max 4h) but we should remove it earlier if all checks pass. Jun, after you open the alert-change PR, put a short description of the validation steps.

jun (sre): will do. I'll also add a note to the alert's runbook explaining acceptable burst behavior and tie to the new dashboard panels for visual validation.

lia (support): customer messages sent and updated: both responded with thanks and said they'll throttle on their side too. 

ops-bot: Incident resolved by maya (oncall). Resolution note: transient cache-rebuild-induced 5xx spike; mitigated via client throttling, serialized cache rebuilds, and short maintenance silence.

maya (oncall): closing out thread. I'll post the incident summary and assign follow-ups. Thanks everyone for quick response. :tada:"
